title: Tim Dooley / Potato of Life — Unified Project Model
purpose: A compact machine-readable model of what the repository is, how its knowledge is produced, where information belongs and how the public atlas should grow.
mission: Recover the whole record, reconstruct the developing thought-system, map its relationships, investigate its sources and consequences, test interpretations against evidence, and preserve what is learned for repair-oriented understanding.
subject: Tim Dooley, the Potato of Life, Potatoism and the wider world of concepts, texts, people, institutions, systems and relationships that the corpus connects to.
core_question: What do we actually have, what does it mean, how did it develop, what is it connected to, what evidence supports it, what remains uncertain, and what consequences follow?

architecture.record: Primary observations, statements, documents, dates and source material.
architecture.canonical: Stable identities and deep dossiers for concepts and entities.
architecture.relationship: Typed edges describing how records connect, depend, transform, influence, contrast or correspond.
architecture.thought: Dated extraction of ideas, directions, questions, signals and concept development.
architecture.reflection: Cross-cutting interpretations and hypotheses generated from multiple records.
architecture.research: External historical, scientific, textual, economic and other evidence used to test or contextualize defined questions.
architecture.presentation: Repository, Timeline, Thought, Dossiers, Books, Scroll and Atlas pages exposing the same underlying knowledge.

coordinates.domain: Independent coordinate: religion, mythology, culture, biology, science, economics, politics, technology, security, geography and other domains.
coordinates.epistemic_status: Independent coordinate: what kind of knowledge or claim the record represents.
coordinates.graph: Independent coordinate: relationships can cross all filing roots, scales, domains and time periods.

consolidation_rule: If several files describe one recurring concept, retain unique provenance and occurrences but resolve identity to one canonical owner. Never create a second identity merely because another layer needs navigation.
depth_rule: A graph edge, alias, URL or short definition is not a dossier. Important concepts need substantial explanation, chronology, relationships, evidence boundaries, uncertainty and research questions.
failure_rule: Missing, unknown, disputed, unavailable and not-yet-researched are explicit states. Build and acquisition failures must never silently become empty datasets or fabricated records.
interpretation_rule: Elegant symbolic correspondence is a research lead, not proof. Historical and scientific claims require evidence appropriate to their domain. Project canon remains identifiable as project canon.
scope_rule: The project can expand from Tim Dooley and Potatoism into religion, mythology, biology, culture, media, institutions, economics, technology, geography and world systems when the corpus or research establishes a meaningful connection. Scope does not justify assuming causation.
end_state: A reader can move from statement → idea → concept → relationship → history → evidence → reflection → consequence and reverse the path back to the originating record without losing provenance.
next_frontier: Backfill the primary Tim Dooley corpus beyond the current supplied 2025–2026 seed.
Attach every thought-archive entry to exact source records or source locations where available.
Build concept mutation timelines for the highest-frequency concepts.
Create a typed thought-transition graph rather than only a concept graph.
Diff older Markdown research against newer machine-readable layers and migrate unique material before deleting anything.
Expose the Thought Archive as a first-class public reading surface.
Strengthen canonical dossiers using the newly reconstructed trajectories instead of creating parallel dossiers.
Use audits to identify duplicate definitions, orphaned relationships, thin records and stale projections before adding new breadth.
